records.rationale: R2Code empirically combines reflective consistency checks with adaptive retrieval to improve requirements-to-code traceability while reducing token use.
LUMEN's industrial IoT cases show specialized LLM agents, knowledge graphs, and human oversight as a transferable observability architecture without a single-agent comparison.
CMCS directly compares collaborative LLM handoffs with constituent single models across eight code benchmarks and quantifies accuracy, scaling, and cost trade-offs.
SemiRALD is a single-agent hybrid anomaly-detection method whose LLM parsing and low-label robustness provide transferable observability and reliability evidence.
This distillation study transfers pseudocode reasoning into smaller code models, providing empirical evidence for a lower-resource alternative to large-model deployment.
This programming-education review evaluates student learning interventions rather than LLM-agent software development or a transferable production mechanism.
ConSelf uses semantic uncertainty and behavioral consensus to reduce noisy self-supervision without teachers or test oracles, a transferable reliability mechanism for code agents.
The title directly identifies an LLM multi-agent software-development system, making it a core retrieval candidate despite the metadata-only abstract.
This empirical human-LLM pair-programming study identifies role switching, prompt quality, context cues, and developer orchestration as practical human-oversight factors.
This communication-science procedure uses coding in the annotation sense and does not address software development or a transferable agent mechanism.
UniTrans uses generated tests, execution feedback, and iterative repair to improve code translation, providing a concrete verification loop for agent workflows.
This primary empirical SE study evaluates developer and tester LLM roles reaching consensus for vulnerability detection and reports sizable precision, recall, and F1 gains.
LDB exposes block-level runtime state to an LLM for stepwise verification and repair, yielding benchmarked debugging gains across several models.
SemGuard detects semantic drift during decoding and rolls back faulty lines, offering model-agnostic real-time verification without tests or execution.
This cross-domain roadmap for generative-AI self-adaptive systems offers indirect MAPE-K and human-on-loop framing but no evaluated SDLC-agent mechanism.
This programming-education mapping concerns teaching roles and learning outcomes rather than production software-agent performance or assurance.
This hybrid privacy check confines LLMs to semantic analysis and uses deterministic knowledge-graph checks, sharply improving accuracy, token cost, and latency.
This perspective on using LLMs to improve evolutionary computation is outside software development and offers no concrete transferable agent mechanism.
KareCoder retrieves curated algorithm knowledge for unfamiliar code tasks and empirically improves Pass@1, supporting external-memory grounding for code agents.
GPTLens empirically compares a role-separated auditor and critic pipeline with one-stage vulnerability detection and exposes the recall and false-positive tension from stochastic sampling.
KPC derives exception-handling failure modes and uses fine-grained check-rewrite prompt chains plus static and dynamic validation to reduce runtime bugs.
This classical k-means seeding paper is unrelated to LLMs, agents, or software-development automation.
This pre-LLM pair-programming process paper provides indirect evidence on driver and observer specialization and collaborative defect detection versus individual programming.
This foundational testing paper indirectly frames formal correctness and empirical fault-revealing strategies but does not study LLM agents.
